# Right of way in the Kestrel Deep

Written by `/research-gaps` because `goal.md` asks for this and no registered
source covers it. Everything below was synthesised from the retrieved page
named in the frontmatter above — it is not the author's own material, and
deleting this folder together with the `right-of-way-research` entry in
`sources.yaml` removes all of it.

## The channel rule

The Kestrel Deep is a narrow channel for the whole of its length between
Torvig and Bellhorn. A vessel proceeding **with** the flood tide keeps the
starboard side of the channel and holds her course; a vessel working against
the tide gives way. The rule is the reverse of the open-water convention on
purpose: a vessel carried by four knots of tide has the least room to
manoeuvre, so she is the one that keeps going.

## Meeting under sail

Between two vessels under sail the tide rule still comes first. Where both are
working the same direction of tide, the vessel on the starboard tack holds her
course. Overtaking is forbidden inside the Deep between the Torvig bar and the
Bellhorn light — the channel is 60 m wide at its narrowest and the soundings
fall away sharply on both sides.

## What is hoisted

A vessel constrained by her draught hoists the black cylinder. In the
archipelago the tide office reads that together with flag **Kell**: taken
together they mean "I cannot leave the channel", and every other vessel gives
way regardless of tack or tide.
